status: In force (since Sep 2024); fees revised Oct 2026
scale: ~3.15 GW registered with Single Buyer (11 RE developers, 8 green consumers) as of May 2026; ~1.3 GW committed by Jun 2025 (DayOne up to 500 MW, Bridge 400 MW, ESR 360 MW, all Johor)
what_it_does: Lets data centres buy solar directly from independent developers over TNB's grid, paying a system access charge (SAC). SAC was 25 sen/kWh at launch, 20 sen from 29 Aug 2025, now 18 sen (14 developer + 4 consumer) for projects online by 31 Dec 2028. All-in CRESS ~48 to 50 sen/kWh vs ~60 sen/kWh grid for DCs.
source_name: The Star 15 Oct 2026; The Star 22 Sep 2026; The Star 16 Jun 2025; W.Media 14 Oct 2026

option: 30% renewable energy rule for data centres
status: Announced (government decision Oct 2026); effective date and scope details not yet published
scale: Kenanga: 12.7 GW incremental DC demand implies ~3.8 GW of green supply at 30%
what_it_does: Requires data centres to use at least 30% renewable power, mainly via CRESS or self-built solar. Legacy projects with signed agreements may be exempt (analyst reading). Energy Commission drafting self-generation guidelines.
source_name: Malay Mail / Bernama 28 Oct 2026; The Star 22 Sep 2026

option: Green Electricity Tariff (GET) and GET GreenPath
what_it_does: TNB sells RE-certified power at a premium, cut from 10 to 20 sen/kWh to 3 to 5 sen/kWh. GreenPath version issues Renewable Energy Certificates aimed at data centre operators and their tenants. Certificate-based, so it does not by itself add new clean capacity.

scale: 2.65 GW solar (lots of 2.2 GW + 300 MW + 150 MW) with 1.25 GW co-located BESS; previous LSS rounds approved over 6 GW since 2016
what_it_does: Adds daytime solar with mandatory batteries, focused on the southern peninsula where data centre load is growing. Up to RM15bn investment.
First large grid-scale BESS in Peninsular Malaysia; shifts solar into evening peak and supports grid stability. Bidders: Blueleaf/Universal Peak, ERS/Gamuda, ERS, Leader Energy.

scale: Contracted 2,346 MW vs actual 1,374 MW (Aug 2026), ~970 MW idle
what_it_does: Electricity Supply Agreements require DCs to declare annual demand and reach 85% of declared maximum demand in the first four years, with a RM8.50/kW monthly shortfall penalty; Connected Load Charge over six years; phased grid access; 10-year demand projections; DCTF approval needs proof of offtake and finance.

scale: Base tariff 39.96 to 45.62 sen/kWh; DCs expected to pay 10% to 14% more before fuel surcharge; ~US$15m to 20m/yr extra for a 100 MW site (consultant estimate)
what_it_does: Unbundles tariff into energy, capacity, network and retail charges plus a monthly fuel surcharge (AFA), so ultra-high voltage users like DCs carry more grid cost instead of households. Not a DC-only surcharge.
Government wants DC backup generators used to shed grid load at critical times or when operating reserves are low. Usually diesel or gas, so it trades emissions for reliability.

option: Sarawak to Peninsula subsea link (Sampadi to Sedenak, Johor)
status: Planned; full feasibility study from Jan 2026
scale: Up to 1,000 MW hydro, ~700 km subsea
date: Pre-feasibility done 2025; no firm COD published
what_it_does: Would bring Sarawak hydropower directly to Johor's data centre corridor. TNB targets 51% local / 49% foreign consortium. Multi-phase.

scale: Up to 100 MW added in EWA Phase 2, taking LTMS-PIP 2.0 to up to 200 MW
what_it_does: Wheels Lao hydropower through Thailand and Malaysia to Singapore. Earns TNB wheeling fees but sends power past Malaysia rather than to its DCs. Malay Mail reported a 30 MW minimum; TNB says up to 100 MW.

option: Malaysia to Singapore exports (Sarawak 1 GW; second interconnector)
scale: Up to 3 GW total; Sarawak to Singapore ~1 GW around 2035; second TNB to SP link up to 2 GW studied
what_it_does: Monetises Malaysian clean power in Singapore. Competes with Johor DCs for the same low-carbon electrons, which cuts against domestic green supply.

date: Decision on whether to include nuclear by 2031
what_it_does: MyPOWER feasibility study (incl. SMRs). No official 2035 nuclear target found; 2035 date in official remarks refers to ~7 GW coal retirement. Could not help before mid-2030s at the earliest.
source_name: The Star 19 Jun 2026; Malay Mail 28 Oct 2026

option: TNB data centre Green Lane and 5,000 MW plan
scale: Support up to 5,000 MW of demand by 2035; connection time cut from 36 to 12 months
what_it_does: Speeds DC grid connections and plans network capacity. Faster connection raises demand growth, so it is a growth tool more than a security fix.

option: MITI Guidelines for Sustainable Development of Data Centre
status: In force for DESAC tax incentive applicants (to 31 Dec 2027)
scale: Design PUE 1.4 hyperscale / 1.6 colocation / 1.7 other; WUE 2.2 m3/MWh
date: Undated document (law firm summaries from Dec 2024)
what_it_does: Requires declared design PUE, CUE and WUE; RE purchase and reclaimed water are optional. Weaker than Singapore.

option: Singapore comparison: DC-CFA2 and Digital Infrastructure Act
status: DC-CFA2 awarded 2026; licensing law passed 7 Oct 2026
scale: 200 MW to 4 operators on Jurong Island (50 MW each); ~280 MW from two tenders vs 1.6 GW hosted
what_it_does: Requires PUE 1.25 at full load, at least 50% green energy, Green Mark Platinum. New law licenses all DCs over 3 MW; IMDA to set PUE and possibly water standards; fines up to S$1m or 10% of turnover.
source_name: King & Wood Mallesons 9 Dec 2025; Eco-Business 8 Oct 2026

scale: Targets 30% digital economy share of GDP, 500,000 digital jobs by 2030
what_it_does: National digital action plan 2026 to 2030 under 'Towards an AI Nation 2030', led by the Digital Ministry; infrastructure pillar names sustainable data centres. No energy or water targets. Distinct from MD Status, MDEC's incentive status (formerly MSC Status) held by DCs such as AirTrunk.
